finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts::webhook signature header name/format is an unverified assumption; a mismatch silently 401s every event and `updatedat` never advances
evidence: I verified the in-repo half: yorkie-signature.guard.ts:48-59 reads `req.header('x-signature-256')` and does a strict length+timingSafeEqual against `sha256=<hex>`, throwing 401 with no accept-path logging, and yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts signs using the same convention as the code under test, so the suite cannot detect a wrong external contract — the claim is accurate about all of that, and about the consequence (silent 401s, updatedAt never advancing from edits). The decisive fact — Yorkie v0.7.12's actual header name — is not in this repository (the Go client is not vendored; only the PR's own docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:47 asserts it), so I could not check it with the tools available. My recollection of Yorkie's webhook client is that the header constant is the Yorkie-specific `X-Signature-Y256` rather than `X-Signature-256`, which would make this a real defect, but that is memory rather than verification, hence low confidence. Note the claim's casing worry is moot — Express's `req.header()` is case-insensitive — so only a literal name/prefix difference matters.
